messages:
Evelyn: Quick sync idea 1 splitting the admit probe into two explicit responsibilities: sampling (what inputs we pick) and orchestration (how we schedule/run benches). tradeoffs?

Ajay: +1. Sampling is policy-heavy and will iterate fast. Orchestration should focus on execution reliability/backpressure.

Leah: Agree. But sampler must guarantee stratification so we don't bias benches and miss regressions.

Tom: Thin contract sounds good: sampler => BatchDescriptor, orchestrator.run(BatchDescriptor) => ResultBundle. Keep it small.

Evelyn: Proposed minimal BatchDescriptor fields: id, payload_uri, features (seqlen, token_count), hints (priority, timeout_ms, force_fresh_kv), provenance (policy_id, sampler_version). Orchestration picks fastpath vs deepbench based on features + hints.

Ravi: Golden samples need stronger invariants. Orchestrator should honor hints like forced seed, no-caching, fixed worker.

Ajay: Example hint set: {priority: smoke|full|golden, force_fresh_kv: true, seed: 1234, timeout_ms: 45000}. Orchestrator doesn't decide sampling, just obeys hints.

Leah: Sampler must return stable identifiers + payload fingerprint so we can reproduce exact runs for postmortems.

Tom: Implementation sketch: sampler svc endpoints: /sample?policy=<id>&size=..., /snapshot?id=...; response contains payload_uri + fingerprint. Orchestrator fetches payload and runs.

Evelyn: Orchestrator config sketch:
```
orchestrator:
  concurrency: 8
  per_tier_capacity: {smoke:4, full:2, golden:2}
  max_retries: 2
  shard_mode: seqlen-aware
```

Ravi: Need tiering so short smoke runs aren't starved by long deep benches. priority queues per tier + capacity enforcement.

Ajay: Failure handling: OOM -> try quantized fallback variant or route to offline slowpath and mark sample flaky. Also emit a "needs-profile" flag back to sampler.

Leah: Observability: sampler emits selection_weights and feature histograms. Orchestrator emits queue depth, run duration, failure reasons, GPU_util tags. Link by batch_id in Console.

Tom: Edge case: central sampler policy is appealing for coverage but is a single-change blast radius. Hybrid: central controller publishes policies; local samplers cache policy and payloads and can operate offline.

Evelyn: Add deployment_mode on BatchDescriptor: hosted | dedicated | private. For private, payload_uri must be local-only and never go to central objectstore. Orchestrator must run in-customer VPC.

Ravi: Use existing KV/objectstore for payloads when allowed. If orchestrator cannot fetch payload -> transient-failure, requeue. If persistent -> mark sample and notify sampler.

Leah: Rollouts: policy changes need shadow sampling window and diff summaries before flip. Sampler should emit rollout diffs.

benchbot: policy-rollout detected. sampler:v2.3 -> v2.4. sample-distribution-delta: {short:+4.2%, long:-3.1%}.

Evelyn: Next steps: draft RFC with API contracts, sample lifecycle, and failure modes. I'll sketch interfaces + PoC orchestrator queues. Volunteers?

Leah: I'll own sampler PoC (central policy + local cache).

Ajay: I'll prototype orchestrator queueing & hint handling.

Evelyn: Thanks — I'll create RFC and link back to this thread.
